articles.title: Plan the Day After Your Event App
articles.excerpt: The event ends. Someone opens the app the next morning to find a photo, while someone else tries an old check-in link. The organizer has moved on to the next event. The software still has to decide wh…
articles.body: The event ends. Someone opens the app the next morning to find a photo, while someone else tries an old check-in link. The organizer has moved on to the next event. The software still has to decide which of those actions should work, and who is responsible for the records that remain. Disclosure: An AI agent researched and drafted this article from my public project documentation and the linked primary sources. The lifecycle design below is a proposed approach, not a claim that these retention controls already exist in From Strangers. I built From Strangers around temporary event communities: phone-based sign-in, a QR check-in pattern, gated participation, shared photos, and event-specific links.

articles.title: Command Authority: Implementing Cross-Tab Observability for Realtime IoT Devices
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for realtime cross-tab coordination in an IoT device control panel, give every tab its own device-scoped credential, let tabs coordinate only who may propose the next command, and make t…
articles.body: Short answer: for realtime cross-tab coordination in an IoT device control panel, give every tab its own device-scoped credential, let tabs coordinate only who may propose the next command, and make the server the sole authority for sequence, deduplication, and acceptance. Build observability signals around that authority path as a small set of causal events. The dashboard can then explain whether a click was blocked by local ownership, rejected by policy, suppressed as a duplicate, sent to the device, or acknowledged. This distinction matters in a B2B SaaS control panel. Cross-tab coordination improves the operator experience, but it isn't an authorization boundary. A background tab can pause, a lease can expire while code is asleep, and two windows can briefly believe they are active.

articles.title: Amoxi: Fast pages with very little JavaScript
articles.excerpt: Server-rendered pages, small interactive islands, links that do not reload, and slow sections that stream in. A typical page is mostly content: headings, text, lists, links. Only a few parts need Java…
articles.body: Server-rendered pages, small interactive islands, links that do not reload, and slow sections that stream in. A typical page is mostly content: headings, text, lists, links. Only a few parts need JavaScript: a search box, a counter, a form that submits without leaving the page. Amoxi is built around that observation. Pages render on the server to plain HTML, and only the interactive parts, called islands, send code to the browser. In this article we add a stats page to the notes app from article 1. It has a filter box that updates as you type, a slow section that streams in, and links that do not reload the page. The whole page costs less than 6 kB of JavaScript.

articles.title: Your AI Agent Has Been Thinking Out Loud This Whole Time
articles.excerpt: Watch an AI agent "think" and you'll notice something wasteful: it writes out every intermediate thought in full English sentences, token by token, before it ever gets to the part that matters — calli…
articles.body: Watch an AI agent "think" and you'll notice something wasteful: it writes out every intermediate thought in full English sentences, token by token, before it ever gets to the part that matters — calling a tool, running code, giving you an answer. That's not reasoning. That's narrating. A paper and open-source release from Stanford, UIUC, and Together AI — dropped days ago, front-paged on Hacker News yesterday — argues the narration was never necessary. It's called HybridAgent , and the pitch is almost rude in its simplicity: let the model think in raw vectors instead of words, and only switch to text when something outside the model actually needs to read it.

The first bug was introduced on 5 August, and two more arose from deployments on 25 and 26 August. Peak: At the worst impacted hour, on 31 August 2025, 16% of Sonnet 4 requests were affected, after a routine load balancing change on 29 August sent more short-context requests to servers configured for a 1M token context window. That is a share of users with at least one bad message, not a share of requests.

articles.body: Book: Event-Driven Architecture Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Sooner or later a pull request like this lands in your queue. It deletes the S3 upload step, base64-encodes the invoice PDF into the message body, and the description reads "SQS takes 1 MiB now, we don't need the bucket." The description is right about the limit. On August 4, 2025, AWS raised the SQS maximum message size from 256 KiB to 1 MiB for standard and FIFO queues, and updated the Lambda event source mapping to match.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.body: Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli arrived at Mars! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

articles.title: NASA Improves Shock, Vibration Analysis
articles.excerpt: Rockets vibrate, shake, and flex intensely as they climb into space, and spacecraft packed with delicate scientific instruments must survive those forces. Before any rocket leaves the ground, NASA eng…
articles.body: Stirling Allen, part of the Dynamic Environments Group with NASA’s Launch Services Program Office, showcases a commercial digital software at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The software performs finite element modeling to support shock and vibration analysis and ensure spacecraft and rockets can withstand harsh vibration, shock, stress, or other physical forces before launch, strengthening mission safety in the process. NASA/Clayton Rougelot Rockets vibrate, shake, and flex intensely as they climb into space, and spacecraft packed with delicate scientific instruments must survive those forces. Before any rocket leaves the ground, NASA engineers work to predict how those stresses will affect every part of a spacecraft.

articles.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
articles.excerpt: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.
articles.body: The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of the unethical and likely illegal acts its agents are performing. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
